name: Lya_1216
text: Lyman alpha (Lya) hydrogen line at rest 1215.7 A. Strongest line in quasar spectra; in DESI coverage (3600-9824 A) it is visible for z between about 1.96 and 7. Seeing a very strong broad peak in the blue end of a spectrum is a classic Lya signature of a high-z QSO. A single strong line interpreted as Lya implies a much higher redshift than the same line interpreted as [OII] or Halpha.

name: CIV_1549
text: CIV broad emission line at rest 1549.1 A, common in quasar spectra. Visible in DESI coverage for z between about 1.32 and 5.3. The Lya-CIV pair is the standard confirmation of a z > 2 QSO: their observed separation ratio 1549.1/1215.7 = 1.274 is fixed.

name: CIII_1909
text: CIII] semi-forbidden emission line at rest 1908.7 A, seen in quasars and AGN. Visible in DESI coverage for z between about 0.89 and 4.1. Together with CIV and MgII it anchors quasar redshifts in the range where Lya has left or not yet entered the optical window.

name: MgII_2799
text: MgII broad emission line at rest 2798.8 A, seen in quasars and some AGN. Visible in DESI coverage for z between about 0.29 and 2.51. Often the only strong broad line for intermediate-redshift QSOs (1 < z < 2), where it can be confused with Halpha or [OII] if treated as a single unidentified line.

name: OII_3727
text: [OII] doublet at rest 3727 A (3726.0 + 3728.8). Primary star-formation tracer and the main redshift feature for DESI ELGs at 0.6 < z < 1.6, where Halpha is out of range. Visible in DESI coverage up to z about 1.63. In single-line spectra [OII] is commonly confused with Halpha: the same observed peak gives z_OII = (1+z_Halpha)*6562.8/3727.1 - 1, a classic misidentification behind catastrophic redshift errors.

name: CaK_3934
text: Calcium K absorption line at rest 3933.7 A. An ABSORPTION feature, strong in passive galaxies and LRGs, bracketing the 4000 A break together with Ca H. Visible in DESI coverage up to z about 1.49. Emission-peak matching does not detect it, so absorption-dominated galaxies can look 'weak' to an emission-line check even at the correct redshift.

name: CaH_3969
text: Calcium H absorption line at rest 3968.5 A, paired with Ca K 3933.7. An ABSORPTION feature typical of passive galaxies and LRGs. Visible in DESI coverage up to z about 1.47. The fixed Ca H+K separation (34.8 A rest) scaled by (1+z) is a reliable redshift anchor for spectra without emission lines.

name: Hdelta_4102
text: Hydrogen Balmer delta line at rest 4101.7 A. Weak in emission; often seen in absorption in post-starburst galaxies. Visible in DESI coverage up to z about 1.39. Rarely useful alone, but adds confirmation when Hbeta and Hgamma are also matched at the same redshift.

name: Hgamma_4340
text: Hydrogen Balmer gamma line at rest 4340.5 A. Visible in DESI coverage up to z about 1.26. Fainter than Hbeta; matching it together with other Balmer lines at a common z is strong evidence, because the Balmer wavelength ratios are fixed by atomic physics.

name: Hbeta_4861
text: Hydrogen Balmer beta line at rest 4861.3 A. Visible in DESI coverage up to z about 1.02. Usually appears together with the [OIII] 4959/5007 pair just redward of it; the Hbeta-[OIII] triplet is one of the most secure low-z redshift anchors in emission-line galaxies.

name: OIII_4959
text: [OIII] forbidden line at rest 4958.9 A, the fainter member of the [OIII] doublet. Visible in DESI coverage up to z about 0.98. Its flux is locked at about 1/3 of [OIII] 5007, so detecting both with that ratio and the fixed 47.9 A rest separation is a strong redshift confirmation.

name: OIII_5007
text: [OIII] forbidden line at rest 5006.8 A, the stronger member of the [OIII] doublet and often the brightest line after Halpha in star-forming galaxies. Visible in DESI coverage up to z about 0.96. A single strong peak can be [OIII] 5007 instead of Halpha: the same observed wavelength then implies a higher redshift by the factor 6562.8/5006.8 = 1.311 applied to (1+z).

name: Halpha_6563
text: Hydrogen Balmer alpha (Halpha) line at rest 6562.8 A. Strongest optical emission line in star-forming galaxies. At z > 0.49 it leaves the DESI optical range (9824 A ceiling), so any z above about 0.5 must be anchored by other lines such as [OII] or [OIII]. Commonly confused with [OII] 3727 and [OIII] 5007 in single-line spectra; that Halpha/[OII] confusion is a leading cause of catastrophic redshift errors.

name: NII_6583
text: [NII] forbidden line at rest 6583.5 A, flanking Halpha (separation 20.7 A rest). Visible in DESI coverage up to z about 0.49. Detecting Halpha with the [NII] lines around it removes the single-line ambiguity, because [OII] and [OIII] have no equivalent close companion at those separations.

name: SII_6716
text: [SII] forbidden doublet member at rest 6716.4 A, redward of Halpha. Visible in DESI coverage up to z about 0.46. Like [NII], its fixed offset from Halpha helps confirm a low-z solution when several of these red lines match peaks simultaneously.
